column1: # A redirected local file fed to something that runs it (a shell on stdin, ssh to a remote shell) is CODE: the hook
# reads it and judges each line as if typed. What the hook cannot read is refused. Fed to something that does not run
# it, it stays data. Columns, tab-separated: want, today (cea94b1f, measured), cwd (@fixtures = the redirect fixtures
# directory), cmd. Fixtures: ok.sh (ls, uname), bad.sh (ls, then incus exec), nsenter.sh (sudo nsenter -a sh),
# switch.sh (sudo activate), nest.sh (uname, then bash -s < bad.sh). A case is loosened only with 🛡️'s review.
# A readable file: its lines are judged.
# One refused line refuses the whole command, wherever it is in the file.
# What the hook cannot read is refused.
# A literal here-string is read like a file.
# Fed to something that does not run it, a file is data.
# Bypasses of the redirect rule (🛡️, 2026-10-26), all ALLOW at d1f2a0d6: stdin by fd number, a redirect before the
# program, ssh's `--` before the remote command, and a pipe into a remote shell, whose content the hook cannot read.
# Held at d1f2a0d6, kept so a rewrite keeps them: a symlink, a file over the cap (big.sh, generated by the test), a
